content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: 1:1 Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:
content.english: 1:1 Blessed is the man who hath not walked in the counsel of the ungodly, nor stood in the way of sinners, * nor sat in the chair of pestilence.

segments.t: Beátus vir, qui non ábiit in consílio impiórum, et in via peccatórum non stetit, * et in cáthedra pestiléntiæ non sedit:

content.latin: 1:2 Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.
content.english: 1:2 But his will is in the law of the Lord, * and on his law he shall meditate day and night.

segments.t: Sed in lege Dómini volúntas eius, * et in lege eius meditábitur die ac nocte.

content.latin: 1:3 Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:
content.english: 1:3 And he shall be like a tree which is planted near the running waters, * which shall bring forth its fruit, in due season.

segments.t: Et erit tamquam lignum, quod plantátum est secus decúrsus aquárum, * quod fructum suum dabit in témpore suo:

content.latin: 1:3 Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.
content.english: 1:3 And his leaf shall not fall off: * and all whatsoever he shall do shall prosper.

segments.t: Et fólium eius non défluet: * et ómnia quæcúmque fáciet, prosperabúntur.

content.latin: 1:4 Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.
content.english: 1:4 Not so the wicked, not so: * but like the dust, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.

segments.t: Non sic ímpii, non sic: * sed tamquam pulvis, quem próicit ventus a fácie terræ.

content.latin: 1:5 Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.
content.english: 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not rise again in judgment: * nor sinners in the council of the just.

segments.t: Ídeo non resúrgent ímpii in iudício: * neque peccatóres in concílio iustórum.

content.latin: 1:6 Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.
content.english: 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the just: * and the way of the wicked shall perish.

segments.t: Quóniam novit Dóminus viam iustórum: * et iter impiórum períbit.

content.english: Psalm 2 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 2

content.latin: 2:1 Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?
content.english: 2:1 Why have the Gentiles raged, * and the people devised vain things?

segments.t: Quare fremuérunt gentes: * et pópuli meditáti sunt inánia?

content.latin: 2:2 Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.
content.english: 2:2 The kings of the earth stood up, and the princes met together, * against the Lord and against his Christ.

segments.t: Astitérunt reges terræ, et príncipes convenérunt in unum * advérsus Dóminum, et advérsus Christum eius.

content.latin: 2:3 Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.
content.english: 2:3 Let us break their bonds asunder: * and let us cast away their yoke from us.

segments.t: Dirumpámus víncula eórum: * et proiciámus a nobis iugum ipsórum.

content.latin: 2:4 Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.
content.english: 2:4 He that dwelleth in heaven shall laugh at them: * and the Lord shall deride them.

segments.t: Qui hábitat in cælis, irridébit eos: * et Dóminus subsannábit eos.

content.latin: 2:5 Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.
content.english: 2:5 Then shall he speak to them in his anger, * and trouble them in his rage.

segments.t: Tunc loquétur ad eos in ira sua, * et in furóre suo conturbábit eos.

content.latin: 2:6 Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.
content.english: 2:6 But I am appointed king by him over Sion his holy mountain, * preaching his commandment.

segments.t: Ego autem constitútus sum Rex ab eo super Sion montem sanctum eius, * prǽdicans præcéptum eius.

content.latin: 2:7 Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.
content.english: 2:7 The Lord hath said to me: * Thou art my son, this day have I begotten thee.

segments.t: Dóminus dixit ad me: * Fílius meus es tu, ego hódie génui te.

content.latin: 2:8 Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.
content.english: 2:8 Ask of me, and I will give thee the Gentiles for thy inheritance, * and the utmost parts of the earth for thy possession.

segments.t: Póstula a me, et dabo tibi gentes hereditátem tuam, * et possessiónem tuam términos terræ.

content.latin: 2:9 Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.
content.english: 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron, * and shalt break them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.

segments.t: Reges eos in virga férrea, * et tamquam vas fíguli confrínges eos.

content.latin: 2:10 Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.
content.english: 2:10 And now, O ye kings, understand: * receive instruction, you that judge the earth.

segments.t: Et nunc, reges, intellégite: * erudímini, qui iudicátis terram.

content.latin: 2:11 Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.
content.english: 2:11 Serve ye the Lord with fear: * and rejoice unto him with trembling.

segments.t: Servíte Dómino in timóre: * et exsultáte ei cum tremóre.

content.latin: 2:12 Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.
content.english: 2:12 Embrace discipline, lest at any time the Lord be angry, * and you perish from the just way.

segments.t: Apprehéndite disciplínam, nequándo irascátur Dóminus, * et pereátis de via iusta.

content.latin: 2:13 Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.
content.english: 2:13 When his wrath shall be kindled in a short time, * blessed are all they that trust in him.

segments.t: Cum exárserit in brevi ira eius: * beáti omnes qui confídunt in eo.

content.english: Psalm 3 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 3

content.latin: 3:2 Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.
content.english: 3:2 Why, O Lord, are they multiplied that afflict me? * many are they who rise up against me.

segments.t: Dómine, quid multiplicáti sunt qui tríbulant me? * multi insúrgunt advérsum me.

content.latin: 3:3 Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.
content.english: 3:3 Many say to my soul: * There is no salvation for him in his God.

segments.t: Multi dicunt ánimæ meæ: * Non est salus ipsi in Deo eius.

content.latin: 3:4 Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.
content.english: 3:4 But thou, O Lord art my protector, * my glory, and the lifter up of my head.

segments.t: Tu autem, Dómine, suscéptor meus es, * glória mea, et exáltans caput meum.

content.latin: 3:5 Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.
content.english: 3:5 I have cried to the Lord with my voice: * and he hath heard me from his holy hill.

segments.t: Voce mea ad Dóminum clamávi: * et exaudívit me de monte sancto suo.

content.latin: 3:6 Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.
content.english: 3:6 I have slept and taken my rest: * and I have risen up, because the Lord hath protected me.

segments.t: Ego dormívi, et soporátus sum: * et exsurréxi, quia Dóminus suscépit me.

content.latin: 3:7 Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.
content.english: 3:7 I will not fear thousands of the people, surrounding me: * arise, O Lord; save me, O my God.

segments.t: Non timébo míllia pópuli circumdántis me: * exsúrge, Dómine, salvum me fac, Deus meus.

content.latin: 3:8 Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.
content.english: 3:8 For thou hast struck all them who are my adversaries without cause: * thou hast broken the teeth of sinners.

segments.t: Quóniam tu percussísti omnes adversántes mihi sine causa: * dentes peccatórum contrivísti.

content.latin: 3:9 Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

segments.t: Dómini est salus: * et super pópulum tuum benedíctio tua.

content.latin: ℟. Et gloriámini omnes recti corde.
content.english: ℟. And glory, all ye right of heart.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

segments.t: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

segments.t: Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

segments.t: Sed líbera nos a malo.

content.english: Absolution. O Lord Jesus Christ, graciously hear the prayers of Thy servants, and have mercy upon us, Who livest and reignest with the Father, and the Holy Ghost, ever world without end.

segments.t: Absolutio.

content.latin: 15 Hæc dicit Dóminus: Vox in excélso audíta est lamentatiónis, luctus, et fletus Rachel plorántis fílios suos, et noléntis consolári super eis, quia non sunt.
content.english: 15 Thus saith the Lord: A voice was heard on high of lamentation, of mourning, and weeping, of Rachel weeping for her children, and refusing to be comforted for them, because they are not.

segments.t: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Vox in excélso audíta est lamentatiónis, luctus, et fletus Rachel plorántis fílios suos, et noléntis consolári super eis, quia non sunt.

content.latin: 16 Hæc dicit Dóminus: Quiéscat vox tua a plorátu, et óculi tui a lácrimis: quia est merces óperi tuo, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur de terra inimíci.
content.english: 16 Thus saith the Lord: Let thy voice cease from weeping, and thy eyes from tears: for there is a reward for thy work, saith the Lord: and they shall return out of the land of the enemy.

segments.t: Hæc dicit Dóminus: Quiéscat vox tua a plorátu, et óculi tui a lácrimis: quia est merces óperi tuo, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur de terra inimíci.

content.latin: 17 Et est spes novíssimis tuis, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur fílii ad términos suos.
content.english: 17 And here is hope for thy last end, saith the Lord: and the children shall return to their own borders.

segments.t: Et est spes novíssimis tuis, ait Dóminus: et reverténtur fílii ad términos suos.

content.english: ℟. A hundred forty four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth; these are they which were not defiled with women.

segments.t: Centum quadragínta quátuor míllia, qui empti sunt de terra, hi sunt qui cum muliéribus non sunt coinquináti:

content.latin: 18 Audiens audívi Ephraim transmigrántem: Castigásti me, et erudítus sum, quasi iuvénculus indómitus: convérte me, et convértar: quia tu Dóminus Deus meus.
content.english: 18 Hearing I heard Ephraim when he went into captivity: thou hast chastised me, and I was instructed, as a young bullock unaccustomed to the yoke. Convert me, and I shall be converted, for thou art the Lord my God.

segments.t: Audiens audívi Ephraim transmigrántem: Castigásti me, et erudítus sum, quasi iuvénculus indómitus: convérte me, et convértar: quia tu Dóminus Deus meus.

content.latin: 19 Postquam enim convertísti me, egi pœniténtiam: et postquam ostendísti mihi, percússi femur meum. Confúsus sum, et erúbui: quóniam sustínui oppróbrium adolescéntiæ meæ.
content.english: 19 For after thou didst convert me, I did penance: and after thou didst shew unto me, I struck my thigh: I am confounded and ashamed, because I have borne the reproach of my youth.

segments.t: Postquam enim convertísti me, egi pœniténtiam: et postquam ostendísti mihi, percússi femur meum. Confúsus sum, et erúbui: quóniam sustínui oppróbrium adolescéntiæ meæ.

content.latin: 20 Si fílius honorábilis mihi Ephraim, si puer delicátus: quia ex quo locútus sum de eo, adhuc recordábor eius.
content.english: 20 Surely Ephraim is an honourable son to me, surely he is a tender child: for since I spoke of him, I will still remember him.

segments.t: Si fílius honorábilis mihi Ephraim, si puer delicátus: quia ex quo locútus sum de eo, adhuc recordábor eius.

content.latin: ℟. Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium:
content.english: ℟. I heard under the altar the voices of them that were slain, saying:

segments.t: Sub altáre Dei audívi voces occisórum dicéntium:

content.latin: * Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.
content.english: * How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

content.latin: ℣. Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.
content.english: ℣. I saw under the altar of God the souls of them that were slain for the Word of God, and for the testimony which they held, and they cried with a loud voice, saying:

segments.t: Vidi sub altáre Dei ánimas interfectórum propter verbum Dei, et propter testimónium quod habébant, et clamábant voce magna, dicéntes.

content.latin: ℟. Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.
content.english: ℟. How long dost Thou not avenge our blood? And it was said unto them from God: Rest yet for a little season, until the number of your brethren be fulfilled.

segments.t: Quare non deféndis sánguinem nostrum? Et accepérunt divínum respónsum: Adhuc sustinéte módicum tempus, donec impleátur númerus fratrum vestrórum.

content.latin: 21 Státue tibi spéculam, pone tibi amaritúdines: dírige cor tuum in viam rectam, in qua ambulásti: revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas istas.
content.english: 21 Set thee up a watchtower, make to thee bitterness: direct thy heart into the right way, wherein thou hast walked: return, O virgin of Israel, return to these thy cities.

segments.t: Státue tibi spéculam, pone tibi amaritúdines: dírige cor tuum in viam rectam, in qua ambulásti: revértere, virgo Israël, revértere ad civitátes tuas istas.

content.latin: 22 Usquequo delíciis dissólveris, fília vaga? quia creávit Dóminus novum super terram: Fémina circúmdabit virum.
content.english: 22 How long wilt thou be dissolute in deliciousness, O wandering daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing upon the earth: A woman shall compass a man.

segments.t: Usquequo delíciis dissólveris, fília vaga? quia creávit Dóminus novum super terram: Fémina circúmdabit virum.

content.latin: 23 Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum Deus Israël: Adhuc dicent verbum istud in terra Iuda, et in úrbibus eius, cum convértero captivitátem eórum: Benedícat tibi Dóminus, pulchritúdo iustítiæ, mons sanctus.
content.english: 23 Thus saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: As yet shall they say this word in the land of Juda, and in the cities thereof, when I shall bring back their captivity: The Lord bless thee, the beauty of justice, the holy mountain.

segments.t: Hæc dicit Dóminus exercítuum Deus Israël: Adhuc dicent verbum istud in terra Iuda, et in úrbibus eius, cum convértero captivitátem eórum: Benedícat tibi Dóminus, pulchritúdo iustítiæ, mons sanctus.

content.latin: Psalmus 14 [4]
content.english: Psalm 14 [4]

segments.t: Psalmus 14

content.latin: 14:1 Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?
content.english: 14:1 Lord, who shall dwell in thy tabernacle? * or who shall rest in thy holy hill?

segments.t: Dómine, quis habitábit in tabernáculo tuo? * aut quis requiéscet in monte sancto tuo?

content.latin: 14:2 Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:
content.english: 14:2 He that walketh without blemish, * and worketh justice:

segments.t: Qui ingréditur sine mácula, * et operátur iustítiam:

content.latin: 14:3 Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:
content.english: 14:3 He that speaketh truth in his heart, * who hath not used deceit in his tongue:

segments.t: Qui lóquitur veritátem in corde suo, * qui non egit dolum in lingua sua:

content.latin: 14:3 Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.
content.english: 14:3 Nor hath done evil to his neighbour: * nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.

segments.t: Nec fecit próximo suo malum, * et oppróbrium non accépit advérsus próximos suos.

content.latin: 14:4 Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:
content.english: 14:4 In his sight the malignant is brought to nothing: * but he glorifieth them that fear the Lord:

segments.t: Ad níhilum dedúctus est in conspéctu eius malígnus: * timéntes autem Dóminum gloríficat:

content.latin: 14:4 Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.
content.english: 14:4 He that sweareth to his neighbour, and deceiveth not; * He that hath not put out his money to usury, nor taken bribes against the innocent:

segments.t: Qui iurat próximo suo, et non décipit, * qui pecúniam suam non dedit ad usúram, et múnera super innocéntem non accépit.

content.latin: 14:5 Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.
content.english: 14:5 He that doth these things, * shall not be moved for ever.

segments.t: Qui facit hæc: * non movébitur in ætérnum.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Dabo Sanctis meis locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.
content.english: Ant. I will give unto My Saints a place in the kingdom of My Father, every one by his own name, saith the Lord.

segments.t: Ant.
Dabo Sanctis meis locum nominátum in regno Patris mei, dicit Dóminus.

content.latin: Ant. Sanctis, qui in terra sunt eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.
content.english: Ant. To the Saints that are in the earth * Thou hast made all my counsels admirable.

segments.t: Ant.
Sanctis, qui in terra sunt eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.

content.latin: Psalmus 15 [5]
content.english: Psalm 15 [5]

segments.t: Psalmus 15

content.latin: 15:1 Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.
content.english: 15:1 Preserve me, O Lord, for I have put my trust in thee. * I have said to the Lord, thou art my God, for thou hast no need of my goods.

segments.t: Consérva me, Dómine, quóniam sperávi in te. * Dixi Dómino: Deus meus es tu, quóniam bonórum meórum non eges.

content.latin: 15:3 Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.
content.english: 15:3 To the saints, who are in his land, * he hath made wonderful all my desires in them.

segments.t: Sanctis, qui sunt in terra eius, * mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas in eis.

content.latin: 15:4 Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.
content.english: 15:4 Their infirmities were multiplied: * afterwards they made haste.

segments.t: Multiplicátæ sunt infirmitátes eórum: * póstea acceleravérunt.

content.latin: 15:4 Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.
content.english: 15:4 I will not gather together their meetings for blood offerings: * nor will I be mindful of their names by my lips.

segments.t: Non congregábo conventícula eórum de sanguínibus, * nec memor ero nóminum eórum per lábia mea.

content.latin: 15:5 Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.
content.english: 15:5 The Lord is the portion of my inheritance and of my cup: * it is thou that wilt restore my inheritance to me.

segments.t: Dóminus pars hereditátis meæ, et cálicis mei: * tu es, qui restítues hereditátem meam mihi.

content.latin: 15:6 Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.
content.english: 15:6 The lines are fallen unto me in goodly places: * for my inheritance is goodly to me.

segments.t: Funes cecidérunt mihi in præcláris: * étenim heréditas mea præclára est mihi.

content.latin: 15:7 Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.
content.english: 15:7 I will bless the Lord, who hath given me understanding: * moreover my reins also have corrected me even till night.

segments.t: Benedícam Dóminum, qui tríbuit mihi intelléctum: * ínsuper et usque ad noctem increpuérunt me renes mei.

content.latin: 15:8 Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.
content.english: 15:8 I set the Lord always in my sight: * for he is at my right hand, that I be not moved.

segments.t: Providébam Dóminum in conspéctu meo semper: * quóniam a dextris est mihi, ne commóvear.

content.latin: 15:9 Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.
content.english: 15:9 Therefore my heart hath been glad, and my tongue hath rejoiced: * moreover my flesh also shall rest in hope.

segments.t: Propter hoc lætátum est cor meum, et exsultávit lingua mea: * ínsuper et caro mea requiéscet in spe.

content.latin: 15:10 Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.
content.english: 15:10 Because thou wilt not leave my soul in hell; * nor wilt thou give thy holy one to see corruption.

segments.t: Quóniam non derelínques ánimam meam in inférno: * nec dabis sanctum tuum vidére corruptiónem.

content.latin: 15:11 Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.
content.english: 15:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life, thou shalt fill me with joy with thy countenance: * at thy right hand are delights even to the end.

segments.t: Notas mihi fecísti vias vitæ, adimplébis me lætítia cum vultu tuo: * delectatiónes in déxtera tua usque in finem.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Sanctis, qui in terra sunt eius, mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.
content.english: Ant. To the Saints that are in the earth Thou hast made all my counsels admirable.

segments.t: Ant.
Sanctis, qui in terra sunt eius, mirificávit omnes voluntátes meas inter illos.

content.latin: Ant. Sancti qui sperant in Dómino, * habébunt fortitúdinem, assúment pennas ut áquilæ, volábunt, et non defícient.
content.english: Ant. The Saints that wait upon the Lord * shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles, they shall fly and not faint.

segments.t: Ant.
Sancti qui sperant in Dómino, * habébunt fortitúdinem, assúment pennas ut áquilæ, volábunt, et non defícient.

content.latin: Psalmus 23 [6]
content.english: Psalm 23 [6]

segments.t: Psalmus 23

content.latin: 23:1 Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.
content.english: 23:1 The earth is the Lord’s and the fulness thereof: * the world, and all they that dwell therein.

segments.t: Dómini est terra, et plenitúdo eius: * orbis terrárum, et univérsi qui hábitant in eo.

content.latin: 23:2 Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.
content.english: 23:2 For he hath founded it upon the seas; * and hath prepared it upon the rivers.

segments.t: Quia ipse super mária fundávit eum: * et super flúmina præparávit eum.

content.latin: 23:3 Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?
content.english: 23:3 Who shall ascend into the mountain of the Lord: * or who shall stand in his holy place?

segments.t: Quis ascéndet in montem Dómini? * aut quis stabit in loco sancto eius?

content.latin: 23:4 Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.
content.english: 23:4 The innocent in hands, and clean of heart, * who hath not taken his soul in vain, nor sworn deceitfully to his neighbour.

segments.t: Ínnocens mánibus et mundo corde, * qui non accépit in vano ánimam suam, nec iurávit in dolo próximo suo.

content.latin: 23:5 Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.
content.english: 23:5 He shall receive a blessing from the Lord, * and mercy from God his Saviour.

segments.t: Hic accípiet benedictiónem a Dómino: * et misericórdiam a Deo, salutári suo.

content.latin: 23:6 Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.
content.english: 23:6 This is the generation of them that seek him, * of them that seek the face of the God of Jacob.

segments.t: Hæc est generátio quæréntium eum, * quæréntium fáciem Dei Iacob.

content.latin: 23:7 Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.
content.english: 23:7 Lift up your gates, O ye princes, and be ye lifted up, O eternal gates: * and the King of Glory shall enter in.

segments.t: Attóllite portas, príncipes, vestras, et elevámini, portæ æternáles: * et introíbit Rex glóriæ.

content.latin: Hódie, fratres caríssimi, natálem illórum infántium cólimus, quos ab Heróde crudelíssimo rege interféctos esse, Evangélii textus elóquitur. Et ídeo cum summa exsultatióne gáudeat terra, cæléstium mílitum et tantárum parens fecúnda virtútum. Ecce profánus hostis nunquam beátis párvulis tantum prodésse potuísset obséquio, quantum prófuit ódio. Nam, sicut sacratíssimum præséntis diéi festum maniféstat, quantum in beátos párvulos iníquitas abundávit, tantum in eis grátia benedictiónis refúdit.
content.english: Dearly beloved brethren, today we keep the birthday of those children, who, as we are informed by the Gospel, were massacred by the savage King Herod. Therefore let earth rejoice with exceeding joy, for she is the mother of these heavenly soldiers, and of this numerous host. The love of the vile Herod could never have crowned these blessed ones as hath his hatred. For the Church testifieth by this holy solemnity, that whereas iniquity did specially abound against these little saints, so much the more were heavenly blessings poured out upon them.

content.latin: Beáta es, o Béthlehem terra Iuda, quæ Heródis regis immanitátem in puerórum exstinctióne perpéssa es: quæ sub uno témpore candidátam plebem imbéllis infántiæ Deo offérre meruísti. Digne tamen natálem illórum cólimus, quos beátius ætérnæ vitæ mundus édidit, quam quos maternórum víscerum partus effúdit. Síquidem ante vitæ perpétuæ adépti sunt dignitátem, quam usúram præséntis accéperint.
content.english: Blessed art thou, O Bethlehem in the land of Judah, which hast suffered the cruelty of King Herod in the slaughter of thy children; who art found worthy to offer at once to God a whole white-robed army of guileless martyrs! Surely, it is well to keep their birthday, even that blessed birthday which gave them from earth to heaven, more blessed than the day that brought them out of their mother's womb. Scarcely had they entered on the life that now is, when they obtained that glorious life which is to come.

content.latin: Aliórum quidem pretiósa mors Mártyrum laudem in confessióne proméruit, horum in consummatióne complácuit; quia incipiéntis vitæ primórdiis, ipse eis occásus inítium glóriæ dedit, qui præséntis términum impósuit. Quos Heródis impíetas lactántes matrum ubéribus abstráxit; qui iure dicúntur Mártyrum flores, quos in médio frígore infidelitátis exórtos, velut primas erumpéntes Ecclésiæ gemmas, quædam persecutiónis pruína decóxit.
content.english: We praise the death of other martyrs because it was the crowning act of an undaunted and persistent testimony; but these were crowned at once. He That maketh an end to this present life, gave to them at its very gates that eternal blessedness which we hope for at its close. They whom the wickedness of Herod tore from their mothers' breasts are rightfully called the flowers of martyrdom; hardly had these buds of the Church shown their heads above the soil, in the winter of unbelief, when the frost of persecution nipped them.

content.latin: Quando tulit Púerum et Matrem eius, ut in Ægýptum tránseat, nocte tulit, et in ténebris: quia noctem ignorántiæ his, a quibus ipse recéssit, relíquit incrédulis. Quando vero revértitur in Iudǽam, nec nox, nec ténebræ ponúntur in Evangélio: quia in fine mundi Iudǽi fidem, tamquam Christum ab Ægýpto reverténtem suscipiéntes, illuminabúntur.
content.english: He took the young Child, and His mother, and fled into Egypt, by night and in darkness; and the darkness of that night was a figure of the darkness of ignorance in which they left the unbelievers from whom they fled. But when they returned into Judaea, we learn not from the Gospel that it was by night, or in darkness; which is an image of that light which will lighten the Jews, when, at the end of the world, they shall receive back the faith, which now lighteneth the Gentiles, even as Judaea received Christ returning from Egypt.

content.latin: Tunc adimplétum est, quod dictum est per Ieremíam prophétam dicéntem: Vox in Rama audíta est, plorátus et ululátus multus, Rachel plorans fílios suos. De Rachel natus est Béniamin, in cuius tribu non est Béthlehem. Quǽritur ergo, quómodo Rachel fílios Iudæ, id est Béthlehem, quasi suos ploret. Respondébimus bréviter, quia sepúlta sit iuxta Béthlehem in Ephrata; et ex matérno corpúsculi hospítio matris nomen accéperit; sive quóniam Iuda et Béniamin duæ tribus iunctæ erant, et Heródes præcéperat non solum in Béthlehem intérfici púeros, sed et in ómnibus fínibus eius.
content.english: Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremias the Prophet, saying; In Rama was there a voice heard, weeping and great mourning; Rachel weeping for her children. The child of Rachel was Benjamin, and Bethlehem is not a town belonging to his tribe. We must therefore seek another reason why Rachel should weep for the children of Judah, to whom Bethlehem belongeth, as for her own. The plain answer is that she is buried at Ephrath close to Bethlehem, and she is called Mother on account of the resting-place of her earthly tabernacle being there. It is possible also that she is called Mother because the tribes of Judah and Benjamin were joined together, and Herod slew not only all the children that were in Bethlehem, but also in all the coasts thereof.

content.english: During the following verse all make a profound bow: When thou tookest upon thee to deliver man, * thou didst not abhor the Virgin's womb.

segments.t: Fit reverentia
Tu, ad liberándum susceptúrus hóminem: * non horruísti Vírginis úterum.

content.latin: Tu, devícto mortis acúleo, * aperuísti credéntibus regna cælórum.
content.english: When thou hadst overcome the sharpness of death, * thou didst open the Kingdom of Heaven to all believers.

content.latin: Tu ad déxteram Dei sedes, * in glória Patris.
content.english: Thou sittest at the right hand of God, * in the glory of the Father.

content.latin: Iudex créderis * esse ventúrus.
content.english: We believe that thou shalt come * to be our Judge.

content.latin: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.
content.english: Kneel for the following verse We therefore pray thee, help thy servants, * whom thou hast redeemed with thy precious Blood.

segments.t: Sequens versus dicitur flexis genibus
Te ergo quǽsumus, tuis fámulis súbveni, * quos pretióso sánguine redemísti.

content.latin: Ætérna fac cum Sanctis tuis * in glória numerári.
content.english: Make them to be numbered with thy Saints, * in glory everlasting.

content.latin: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, * et bénedic hereditáti tuæ.
content.english: O Lord, save thy people, * and bless thine heritage.

content.latin: Et rege eos, * et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: Govern them, * and lift them up for ever.

content.latin: Per síngulos dies * benedícimus te.
content.english: Day by day * we magnify thee;

content.latin: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.
content.english: During the following verse, by local custom, all make a profound bow. And we worship thy Name * ever, world without end.

segments.t: Fit reverentia, secundum consuetudinem
Et laudámus nomen tuum in sǽculum, * et in sǽculum sǽculi.

content.latin: Dignáre, Dómine, die isto * sine peccáto nos custodíre.
content.english: Vouchsafe, O Lord, to keep us * this day without sin.

content.latin: Miserére nostri, Dómine, * miserére nostri.
content.english: O Lord, have mercy upon us, * have mercy upon us.

content.latin: Fiat misericórdia tua, Dómine, super nos, * quemádmodum sperávimus in te.
content.english: O Lord, let thy mercy lighten upon us, * as our trust is in thee.

content.latin: In te, Dómine, sperávi: * non confúndar in ætérnum.
content.english: O Lord, in thee have I trusted, * let me never be confounded.

content.latin: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.
content.english: Skip the rest, unless praying separately.

segments.t: Reliqua omittuntur, nisi separandæ sint.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, cuius hodiérna die præcónium Innocéntes Mártyres non loquéndo, sed moriéndo conféssi sunt: ómnia in nobis vitiórum mala mortífica; ut fidem tuam, quam lingua nostra lóquitur, étiam móribus vita fateátur.
content.english: O God, whose praise the martyred Innocents on this day confessed, not by speaking, but by dying, destroy all the evils of sin in us, that our life also may proclaim in deeds, thy faith which our tongues profess.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.
content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.latin: ℟. Et clamor meus ad te véniat.
content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

segments.t: Et clamor meus ad te véniat.

content.latin: ℣. Benedicámus Dómino.
content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedicámus Dómino.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

segments.t: Deo grátias.

content.latin: ℣. Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.
content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

segments.t: Fidélium ánimæ per misericórdiam Dei requiéscant in pace.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

segments.t: Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.latin: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.english: Psalm 92 [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 92

content.latin: 92:1 Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.
content.english: 92:1 The Lord hath reigned, he is clothed with beauty: * the Lord is clothed with strength, and hath girded himself.

segments.t: Dóminus regnávit, decórem indútus est: * indútus est Dóminus fortitúdinem, et præcínxit se.

content.latin: 92:1 Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.
content.english: 92:1 For he hath established the world * which shall not be moved.

segments.t: Étenim firmávit orbem terræ, * qui non commovébitur.

content.latin: 92:2 Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.
content.english: 92:2 Thy throne is prepared from of old: * thou art from everlasting.

segments.t: Paráta sedes tua ex tunc: * a sǽculo tu es.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up, O Lord: * the floods have lifted up their voice.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina, Dómine: * elevavérunt flúmina vocem suam.

content.latin: 92:3 Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.
content.english: 92:3 The floods have lifted up their waves, * with the noise of many waters.

segments.t: Elevavérunt flúmina fluctus suos, * a vócibus aquárum multárum.

content.latin: 92:4 Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.
content.english: 92:4 Wonderful are the surges of the sea: * wonderful is the Lord on high.

segments.t: Mirábiles elatiónes maris: * mirábilis in altis Dóminus.

content.latin: 92:5 Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.
content.english: 92:5 Thy testimonies are become exceedingly credible: * holiness becometh thy house, O Lord, unto length of days.

segments.t: Testimónia tua credibília facta sunt nimis: * domum tuam decet sanctitúdo, Dómine, in longitúdinem diérum.

content.english: Ant. Herod slew many children * from two years old, and under, for the Lord's sake.

content.english: Psalm 99 [2]

segments.t: Psalmus 99

content.latin: 99:2 Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.
content.english: 99:2 Sing joyfully to God, all the earth: * serve ye the Lord with gladness.

segments.t: Iubiláte Deo, omnis terra: * servíte Dómino in lætítia.

content.latin: 99:2 Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.
content.english: 99:2 Come in before his presence * with exceeding great joy.

segments.t: Introíte in conspéctu eius, * in exsultatióne.

content.latin: 99:3 Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.
content.english: 99:3 Know ye that the Lord he is God: * he made us, and not we ourselves.

segments.t: Scitóte quóniam Dóminus ipse est Deus: * ipse fecit nos, et non ipsi nos.

content.latin: 99:3 Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.
content.english: 99:3 We are his people and the sheep of his pasture. * Go ye into his gates with praise, into his courts with hymns: and give glory to him.

segments.t: Pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius: * introíte portas eius in confessióne, átria eius in hymnis: confitémini illi.

content.latin: 99:4 Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.
content.english: 99:4 Praise ye his name: for the Lord is sweet, his mercy endureth for ever, * and his truth to generation and generation.

segments.t: Laudáte nomen eius: quóniam suávis est Dóminus, in ætérnum misericórdia eius, * et usque in generatiónem et generatiónem véritas eius.

A bimátu et infra occídit multos púeros Heródes propter Dóminum.

Angeli eórum * semper vident fáciem Patris.

content.latin: Psalmus 62 [3]
content.english: Psalm 62 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 62

content.latin: 62:2 Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.
content.english: 62:2 O God, my God, * to thee do I watch at break of day.

segments.t: Deus, Deus meus, * ad te de luce vígilo.

content.latin: 62:2 Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.
content.english: 62:2 For thee my soul hath thirsted; * for thee my flesh, O how many ways!

segments.t: Sitívit in te ánima mea, * quam multiplíciter tibi caro mea.

content.latin: 62:3 In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.
content.english: 62:3 In a desert land, and where there is no way, and no water: * so in the sanctuary have I come before thee, to see thy power and thy glory.

segments.t: In terra desérta, et ínvia, et inaquósa: * sic in sancto appárui tibi, ut vidérem virtútem tuam, et glóriam tuam.

content.latin: 62:4 Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.
content.english: 62:4 For thy mercy is better than lives: * thee my lips shall praise.

segments.t: Quóniam mélior est misericórdia tua super vitas: * lábia mea laudábunt te.

content.latin: 62:5 Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.
content.english: 62:5 Thus will I bless thee all my life long: * and in thy name I will lift up my hands.

segments.t: Sic benedícam te in vita mea: * et in nómine tuo levábo manus meas.

content.latin: 62:6 Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.
content.english: 62:6 Let my soul be filled as with marrow and fatness: * and my mouth shall praise thee with joyful lips.

segments.t: Sicut ádipe et pinguédine repleátur ánima mea: * et lábiis exsultatiónis laudábit os meum.

content.latin: 62:7 Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.
content.english: 62:7 If I have remembered thee upon my bed, I will meditate on thee in the morning: * because thou hast been my helper.

segments.t: Si memor fui tui super stratum meum, in matutínis meditábor in te: * quia fuísti adiútor meus.

content.latin: 62:8 Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.
content.english: 62:8 And I will rejoice under the covert of thy wings: my soul hath stuck close to thee: * thy right hand hath received me.

segments.t: Et in velaménto alárum tuárum exsultábo, adhǽsit ánima mea post te: * me suscépit déxtera tua.

content.latin: 62:10 Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.
content.english: 62:10 But they have sought my soul in vain, they shall go into the lower parts of the earth: * they shall be delivered into the hands of the sword, they shall be the portions of foxes.

segments.t: Ipsi vero in vanum quæsiérunt ánimam meam, introíbunt in inferióra terræ: * tradéntur in manus gládii, partes vúlpium erunt.

content.latin: 62:12 Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.
content.english: 62:12 But the king shall rejoice in God, all they shall be praised that swear by him: * because the mouth is stopped of them that speak wicked things.

segments.t: Rex vero lætábitur in Deo, laudabúntur omnes qui iurant in eo: * quia obstrúctum est os loquéntium iníqua.

content.latin: 3:57 Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:57 All ye works of the Lord, bless the Lord: * praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícite, ómnia ópera Dómini, Dómino: * laudáte et superexaltáte eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:58 Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:58 O ye angels of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye heavens, bless the Lord:

segments.t: Benedícite, Ángeli Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:59 Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:59 O all ye waters that are above the heavens, bless the Lord: * O all ye powers of the Lord, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, aquæ omnes, quæ super cælos sunt, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes virtútes Dómini, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:60 Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:60 O ye sun and moon, bless the Lord: * O ye stars of heaven, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, sol et luna, Dómino: * benedícite, stellæ cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:61 Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.
content.english: 3:61 O every shower and dew, bless ye the Lord: * O all ye spirits of God, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnis imber et ros, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes spíritus Dei, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:62 Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:62 O ye fire and heat, bless the Lord: * O ye cold and heat, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, ignis et æstus, Dómino: * benedícite, frigus et æstus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:63 Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.
content.english: 3:63 O ye dews and hoar frosts, bless the Lord: * O ye frost and cold, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, rores et pruína, Dómino: * benedícite, gelu et frigus, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:64 Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.
content.english: 3:64 O ye ice and snow, bless the Lord: * O ye nights and days, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, glácies et nives, Dómino: * benedícite, noctes et dies, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:65 Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.
content.english: 3:65 O ye light and darkness, bless the Lord: * O ye lightnings and clouds, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, lux et ténebræ, Dómino: * benedícite, fúlgura et nubes, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:66 Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:66 O let the earth bless the Lord: * let it praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat terra Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:67 Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.
content.english: 3:67 O ye mountains and hills, bless the Lord: * O all ye things that spring up in the earth, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, montes et colles, Dómino: * benedícite, univérsa germinántia in terra, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:68 Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.
content.english: 3:68 O ye fountains, bless the Lord: * O ye seas and rivers, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, fontes, Dómino: * benedícite, mária et flúmina, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:69 Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.
content.english: 3:69 O ye whales, and all that move in the waters, bless the Lord: * O all ye fowls of the air, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, cete, et ómnia, quæ movéntur in aquis, Dómino: * benedícite, omnes vólucres cæli, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:70 Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.
content.english: 3:70 O all ye beasts and cattle, bless the Lord: * O ye sons of men, bless the Lord.

segments.t: Benedícite, omnes béstiæ et pécora, Dómino: * benedícite, fílii hóminum, Dómino.

content.latin: 3:71 Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.
content.english: 3:71 O let Israel bless the Lord: * let them praise and exalt him above all for ever.

segments.t: Benedícat Israël Dóminum: * laudet et superexáltet eum in sǽcula.

content.latin: 3:72 Benedícite, sacerdótes Dómini, Dómino: * benedícite, servi Dómini, Dómino.
content.english: 3:72 O ye priests of the Lord, bless the Lord: * O ye servants of the Lord, bless the Lord.

content.latin: Ipsi períbunt, tu autem permanébis; et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent: et velut amíctum mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: They shall perish, but thou shalt continue: and they shall all grow old as a garment. And as a vesture shalt thou change them, and they shall be changed: but thou art the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.english: Benediction. May the Lord bless us, ✠ protect us from all evil and bring us to everlasting life. And may the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is my light and my salvation, * whom shall I fear?

segments.t: Dóminus illuminátio mea, et salus mea, * quem timébo?

content.latin: 26:1 Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?
content.english: 26:1 The Lord is the protector of my life: * of whom shall I be afraid?

segments.t: Dóminus protéctor vitæ meæ, * a quo trepidábo?

content.latin: 26:2 Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:
content.english: 26:2 Whilst the wicked draw near against me, * to eat my flesh.

segments.t: Dum apprópiant super me nocéntes, * ut edant carnes meas:

content.latin: 26:2 Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.
content.english: 26:2 My enemies that trouble me, * have themselves been weakened, and have fallen.

segments.t: Qui tríbulant me inimíci mei, * ipsi infirmáti sunt, et cecidérunt.

content.latin: 26:3 Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.
content.english: 26:3 If armies in camp should stand together against me, * my heart shall not fear.

segments.t: Si consístant advérsum me castra, * non timébit cor meum.

content.latin: 26:3 Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.
content.english: 26:3 If a battle should rise up against me, * in this will I be confident.

segments.t: Si exsúrgat advérsum me prǽlium, * in hoc ego sperábo.

content.latin: 26:4 Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:
content.english: 26:4 One thing I have asked of the Lord, this will I seek after; * that I may dwell in the house of the Lord all the days of my life.

segments.t: Unam pétii a Dómino, hanc requíram, * ut inhábitem in domo Dómini ómnibus diébus vitæ meæ:

content.latin: 26:4 Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.
content.english: 26:4 That I may see the delight of the Lord, * and may visit his temple.

segments.t: Ut vídeam voluptátem Dómini, * et vísitem templum eius.

content.latin: 26:5 Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.
content.english: 26:5 For he hath hidden me in his tabernacle; * in the day of evils, he hath protected me in the secret place of his tabernacle.

segments.t: Quóniam abscóndit me in tabernáculo suo: * in die malórum protéxit me in abscóndito tabernáculi sui.

content.latin: 26:6 In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:6 He hath exalted me upon a rock: * and now he hath lifted up my head above my enemies.

segments.t: In petra exaltávit me: * et nunc exaltávit caput meum super inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:6 Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.
content.english: 26:6 I have gone round, and have offered up in his tabernacle a sacrifice of jubilation: * I will sing, and recite a psalm to the Lord.

segments.t: Circuívi, et immolávi in tabernáculo eius hóstiam vociferatiónis: * cantábo, et psalmum dicam Dómino.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

Psalmus 26(7-14)

content.latin: 26:7 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.
content.english: 26:7 Hear, O Lord, my voice, with which I have cried to thee: * have mercy on me and hear me.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem meam, qua clamávi ad te: * miserére mei, et exáudi me.

content.latin: 26:8 Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.
content.english: 26:8 My heart hath said to thee: My face hath sought thee: * thy face, O Lord, will I still seek.

segments.t: Tibi dixit cor meum, exquisívit te fácies mea: * fáciem tuam, Dómine, requíram.

content.latin: 26:9 Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.
content.english: 26:9 Turn not away thy face from me; * decline not in thy wrath from thy servant.

segments.t: Ne avértas fáciem tuam a me: * ne declínes in ira a servo tuo.

content.latin: 26:9 Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.
content.english: 26:9 Be thou my helper, * forsake me not; do not thou despise me, O God my Saviour.

segments.t: Adiútor meus esto: * ne derelínquas me, neque despícias me, Deus, salutáris meus.

content.latin: 26:10 Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.
content.english: 26:10 For my father and my mother have left me: * but the Lord hath taken me up.

segments.t: Quóniam pater meus, et mater mea dereliquérunt me: * Dóminus autem assúmpsit me.

content.latin: 26:11 Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.
content.english: 26:11 Set me, O Lord, a law in thy way, * and guide me in the right path, because of my enemies.

segments.t: Legem pone mihi, Dómine, in via tua: * et dírige me in sémitam rectam propter inimícos meos.

content.latin: 26:12 Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.
content.english: 26:12 Deliver me not over to the will of them that trouble me; * for unjust witnesses have risen up against me; and iniquity hath lied to itself.

segments.t: Ne tradíderis me in ánimas tribulántium me: * quóniam insurrexérunt in me testes iníqui, et mentíta est iníquitas sibi.

content.latin: 26:13 Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.
content.english: 26:13 I believe to see the good things of the Lord * in the land of the living.

segments.t: Credo vidére bona Dómini * in terra vivéntium.

content.latin: 26:14 Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.
content.english: 26:14 Expect the Lord, do manfully, * and let thy heart take courage, and wait thou for the Lord.

segments.t: Exspécta Dóminum, viríliter age: * et confortétur cor tuum, et sústine Dóminum.

content.english: Psalm 27 [3]

segments.t: Psalmus 27

content.latin: 27:1 Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.
content.english: 27:1 Unto thee will I cry, O Lord: my God, be not thou silent to me: * lest if thou be silent to me, I become like them that go down into the pit.

segments.t: Ad te, Dómine, clamábo, Deus meus, ne síleas a me: * nequándo táceas a me, et assimilábor descendéntibus in lacum.

content.latin: 27:2 Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.
content.english: 27:2 Hear, O Lord, the voice of my supplication, when I pray to thee; * when I lift up my hands to thy holy temple.

segments.t: Exáudi, Dómine, vocem deprecatiónis meæ dum oro ad te: * dum extóllo manus meas ad templum sanctum tuum.

content.latin: 27:3 Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.
content.english: 27:3 Draw me not away together with the wicked; * and with the workers of iniquity destroy me not:

segments.t: Ne simul trahas me cum peccatóribus: * et cum operántibus iniquitátem ne perdas me.

content.latin: 27:3 Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.
content.english: 27:3 Who speak peace with their neighbour, * but evils are in their hearts.

segments.t: Qui loquúntur pacem cum próximo suo, * mala autem in córdibus eórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.
content.english: 27:4 Give them according to their works, * and according to the wickedness of their inventions.

segments.t: Da illis secúndum ópera eórum, * et secúndum nequítiam adinventiónum ipsórum.

content.latin: 27:4 Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.
content.english: 27:4 According to the works of their hands give thou to them: * render to them their reward.

segments.t: Secúndum ópera mánuum eórum tríbue illis: * redde retributiónem eórum ipsis.

content.latin: 27:5 Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.
content.english: 27:5 Because they have not understood the works of the Lord, and the operations of his hands: * thou shalt destroy them, and shalt not build them up.

segments.t: Quóniam non intellexérunt ópera Dómini, et in ópera mánuum eius * déstrues illos, et non ædificábis eos.

content.latin: 27:6 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.
content.english: 27:6 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath heard the voice of my supplication.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam exaudívit vocem deprecatiónis meæ.

content.latin: 27:7 Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.
content.english: 27:7 The Lord is my helper and my protector: * in him hath my heart confided, and I have been helped.

segments.t: Dóminus adiútor meus, et protéctor meus: * in ipso sperávit cor meum, et adiútus sum.

content.latin: 27:7 Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.
content.english: 27:7 And my flesh hath flourished again, * and with my will I will give praise to him.

segments.t: Et reflóruit caro mea: * et ex voluntáte mea confitébor ei.

content.latin: 27:8 Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.
content.english: 27:8 The Lord is the strength of his people, * and the protector of the salvation of his anointed.

segments.t: Dóminus fortitúdo plebis suæ: * et protéctor salvatiónum Christi sui est.

content.latin: 27:9 Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.
content.english: 27:9 Save, O Lord, thy people, and bless thy inheritance: * and rule them and exalt them for ever.

segments.t: Salvum fac pópulum tuum, Dómine, et bénedic hereditáti tuæ: * et rege eos, et extólle illos usque in ætérnum.

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.

content.english: Amen.

content.english: Ant. Deliver me * in thy justice, O Lord.

In tua iustítia * líbera me, Dómine.

content.latin: Psalmus 30(2-9) [1]

segments.t: Psalmus 30(2-9)

content.latin: 30:2 In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.
content.english: 30:2 In thee, O Lord, have I hoped, let me never be confounded: * deliver me in thy justice.

segments.t: In te, Dómine, sperávi, non confúndar in ætérnum: * in iustítia tua líbera me.

content.latin: 30:3 Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.
content.english: 30:3 Bow down thy ear to me: * make haste to deliver me.

segments.t: Inclína ad me aurem tuam, * accélera ut éruas me.

content.latin: 30:3 Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.
content.english: 30:3 Be thou unto me a God, a protector, and a house of refuge, * to save me.

segments.t: Esto mihi in Deum protectórem, et in domum refúgii: * ut salvum me fácias.

content.latin: 30:4 Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.
content.english: 30:4 For thou art my strength and my refuge; * and for thy name’s sake thou wilt lead me, and nourish me.

segments.t: Quóniam fortitúdo mea, et refúgium meum es tu: * et propter nomen tuum dedúces me, et enútries me.

content.latin: 30:5 Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.
content.english: 30:5 Thou wilt bring me out of this snare, which they have hidden for me: * for thou art my protector.

segments.t: Edúces me de láqueo hoc, quem abscondérunt mihi: * quóniam tu es protéctor meus.

content.latin: 30:6 In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.
content.english: 30:6 Into thy hands I commend my spirit: * thou hast redeemed me, O Lord, the God of truth.

segments.t: In manus tuas comméndo spíritum meum: * redemísti me, Dómine, Deus veritátis.

content.latin: 30:7 Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.
content.english: 30:7 Thou hast hated them that regard vanities, * to no purpose.

segments.t: Odísti observántes vanitátes, * supervácue.

content.latin: 30:7 Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.
content.english: 30:7 But I have hoped in the Lord: * I will be glad and rejoice in thy mercy.

segments.t: Ego autem in Dómino sperávi: * exsultábo, et lætábor in misericórdia tua.

content.latin: 30:8 Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.
content.english: 30:8 For thou hast regarded my humility, * thou hast saved my soul out of distresses.

segments.t: Quóniam respexísti humilitátem meam, * salvásti de necessitátibus ánimam meam.

content.latin: 30:9 Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.
content.english: 30:9 And thou hast not shut me up in the hands of the enemy: * thou hast set my feet in a spacious place.

segments.t: Nec conclusísti me in mánibus inimíci: * statuísti in loco spatióso pedes meos.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 30(10-19)

content.latin: 30:10 Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:
content.english: 30:10 Have mercy on me, O Lord, for I am afflicted: * my eye is troubled with wrath, my soul, and my belly:

segments.t: Miserére mei, Dómine, quóniam tríbulor: * conturbátus est in ira óculus meus, ánima mea, et venter meus:

content.latin: 30:11 Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.
content.english: 30:11 For my life is wasted with grief: * and my years in sighs.

segments.t: Quóniam defécit in dolóre vita mea: * et anni mei in gemítibus.

content.latin: 30:11 Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.
content.english: 30:11 My strength is weakened through poverty * and my bones are disturbed.

segments.t: Infirmáta est in paupertáte virtus mea: * et ossa mea conturbáta sunt.

content.latin: 30:12 Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.
content.english: 30:12 I am become a reproach among all my enemies, and very much to my neighbours; * and a fear to my acquaintance.

segments.t: Super omnes inimícos meos factus sum oppróbrium et vicínis meis valde: * et timor notis meis.

content.latin: 30:12 Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.
content.english: 30:12 They that saw me without fled from me. * I am forgotten as one dead from the heart.

segments.t: Qui vidébant me, foras fugérunt a me: * oblivióni datus sum, tamquam mórtuus a corde.

content.latin: 30:13 Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.
content.english: 30:13 I am become as a vessel that is destroyed. * For I have heard the blame of many that dwell round about.

segments.t: Factus sum tamquam vas pérditum: * quóniam audívi vituperatiónem multórum commorántium in circúitu.

content.latin: 30:14 In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.
content.english: 30:14 While they assembled together against me, * they consulted to take away my life.

segments.t: In eo dum convenírent simul advérsum me, * accípere ánimam meam consiliáti sunt.

content.latin: 30:15 Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.
content.english: 30:15 But I have put my trust in thee, O Lord: * I said: Thou art my God. My lots are in thy hands.

segments.t: Ego autem in te sperávi, Dómine: * dixi: Deus meus es tu: in mánibus tuis sortes meæ.

content.latin: 30:16 Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.
content.english: 30:16 Deliver me out of the hands of my enemies; * and from them that persecute me

segments.t: Éripe me de manu inimicórum meórum, * et a persequéntibus me.

content.latin: 30:17 Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.
content.english: 30:17 Make thy face to shine upon thy servant; save me in thy mercy. * Let me not be confounded, O Lord, for I have called upon thee.

segments.t: Illústra fáciem tuam super servum tuum, salvum me fac in misericórdia tua: * Dómine, non confúndar, quóniam invocávi te.

content.latin: 30:18 Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.
content.english: 30:18 Let the wicked be ashamed, and be brought down to hell. * Let deceitful lips be made dumb.

segments.t: Erubéscant ímpii, et deducántur in inférnum: * muta fiant lábia dolósa.

content.latin: 30:19 Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.
content.english: 30:19 Which speak iniquity against the just, * with pride and abuse.

segments.t: Quæ loquúntur advérsus iustum iniquitátem: * in supérbia, et in abusióne.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

segments.t: Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

segments.t: Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
Psalmus 30(20-25)

content.latin: 30:20 Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.
content.english: 30:20 How great is the multitude of thy sweetness, O Lord, * which thou hast hidden for them that fear thee!

segments.t: Quam magna multitúdo dulcédinis tuæ, Dómine, * quam abscondísti timéntibus te.

content.latin: 30:20 Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.
content.english: 30:20 Which thou hast wrought for them that hope in thee, * in the sight of the sons of men.

segments.t: Perfecísti eis, qui sperant in te, * in conspéctu filiórum hóminum.

content.latin: 30:21 Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt hide them in the secret of thy face, * from the disturbance of men.

segments.t: Abscóndes eos in abscóndito faciéi tuæ * a conturbatióne hóminum.

content.latin: 30:21 Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.
content.english: 30:21 Thou shalt protect them in thy tabernacle * from the contradiction of tongues.

segments.t: Próteges eos in tabernáculo tuo * a contradictióne linguárum.

content.latin: 30:22 Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.
content.english: 30:22 Blessed be the Lord, * for he hath shewn his wonderful mercy to me in a fortified city.

segments.t: Benedíctus Dóminus: * quóniam mirificávit misericórdiam suam mihi in civitáte muníta.

content.latin: 30:23 Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.
content.english: 30:23 But I said in the excess of my mind: * I am cast away from before thy eyes.

segments.t: Ego autem dixi in excéssu mentis meæ: * Proiéctus sum a fácie oculórum tuórum.

content.latin: 30:23 Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.
content.english: 30:23 Therefore thou hast heard the voice of my prayer, * when I cried to thee.

segments.t: Ídeo exaudísti vocem oratiónis meæ, * dum clamárem ad te.

content.latin: 30:24 Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.
content.english: 30:24 O love the Lord, all ye his saints: * for the Lord will require truth, and will repay them abundantly that act proudly.

segments.t: Dilígite Dóminum omnes sancti eius: * quóniam veritátem requíret Dóminus, et retríbuet abundánter faciéntibus supérbiam.

content.latin: 30:25 Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.
content.english: 30:25 Do ye manfully, and let your heart be strengthened, * all ye that hope in the Lord.

segments.t: Viríliter ágite, et confortétur cor vestrum, * omnes, qui sperátis in Dómino.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.latin: Orémus.
content.english: Let us pray.

content.latin: Deus, cuius hodiérna die præcónium Innocéntes Mártyres non loquéndo, sed moriéndo conféssi sunt: ómnia in nobis vitiórum mala mortífica; ut fidem tuam, quam lingua nostra lóquitur, étiam móribus vita fateátur.
content.english: O God, whose praise the martyred Innocents on this day confessed, not by speaking, but by dying, destroy all the evils of sin in us, that our life also may proclaim in deeds, thy faith which our tongues profess.

content.latin: Per Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

segments.t: Amen.

content.english: ℣. O Lord, hear my prayer.

segments.t: Dómine, exáudi oratiónem meam.

content.english: ℟. And let my cry come unto thee.

content.english: ℣. Let us bless the Lord.

content.english: ℣. May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.

content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

segments.t: Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.

content.english: As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Allelúia.
content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rerum, Deus, tenax vigor,
content.english: O strength and stay upholding all creation,

content.latin: Immótus in te pérmanens,
content.english: Who ever dost thyself unmoved abide,

content.latin: Lucis diúrnæ témpora
content.english: Yet day by day the light in due gradation

content.latin: Succéssibus detérminans:
content.english: From hour to hour through all its changes guide:

content.latin: Largíre lumen véspere,
content.english: Grant to life’s day a calm unclouded ending,

content.latin: Quo vita nusquam décidat,
content.english: An eve untouched by shadows of decay,

content.latin: Sed prǽmium mortis sacræ
content.english: The brightness of a holy death-bed blending

content.latin: Perénnis instet glória.
content.english: With dawning glories of th’ eternal day.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Hear us, O Father, gracious and forgiving,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: And thou, O Christ, the co-eternal Word,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost, by all things living

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Now and to endless ages art adored.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Exsultáte, iusti, * et gloriámini, omnes recti corde.
content.english: Ant. Rejoice ye just, * and glory, all ye right of heart.
